title: National Works on Paper 2026 (NWOP)
summary: MPRG's biennial $20,000 acquisitive survey of contemporary Australian work on paper: prints, drawings, collage, mixed media. Free, Tue to Sun 11am to 4pm.
nearbyAttractions: Mornington Main Street; Mornington Park; Peninsula Hot Springs
suggestedItineraryPairing: Gallery visit then lunch on Main Street; pair with wine at a local cellar door
editorVerdict: National Works on Paper is the show that justifies MPRG's quietly serious reputation, and the only Peninsula exhibition that pulls a genuinely national field.
editorNote:
NWOP is one of Australia's longest-running prizes for work on paper: prints, drawings, collage, mixed media. The $20,000 major acquisition (plus a swag of smaller awards and acquisitions) is enough to draw entries from artists who would otherwise never list a Mornington venue. Held every two years, it is the closest thing the Peninsula has to a destination art event.

Go for the opening if you care about meeting the artists and seeing the prize call. Otherwise the show runs to 22 November and rewards a quiet Tuesday or a wet Sunday more than a busy Saturday. Free entry, no booking for the show itself.

The practical pairing is obvious: gallery first, lunch on Main Street, an afternoon cellar door if the weather is on. Budget ninety minutes for the show alone if you read every label.
